steps.title: Three villages
steps.body: Barbaresco DOCG lies north-east of Alba, near the Tanaro river, mainly in three villages: Barbaresco, Neive and Treiso. It's smaller than Barolo, about 750 hectares compared with about 2,200. It's slightly lower and warmer, closer to the river, so Nebbiolo ripens a little earlier.

steps.title: Rules and style
steps.body: Barbaresco must be 100% Nebbiolo, aged at least 26 months, 9 in wood; Riserva 50 months. It has 66 MGAs, like Asili, Rabajà and Montestefano. Its wines are often described as more elegant and approachable earlier than Barolo, with softer tannins, though site and producer matter more.

steps.prompt: How does Barbaresco's minimum ageing compare with Barolo's?

steps.title: Producers
steps.body: Angelo Gaja, from the 1960s, raised Barbaresco's global prestige, with single-vineyard wines and new ideas. The Produttori del Barbaresco, a co-operative founded in 1958, makes some of the best-value fine wines in Italy, including single-vineyard Riservas. Bruno Giacosa was another legend.
